newsitem.title: USA: U.S. safety board sets hearing on ValuJet crash.
newsitem.headline: U.S. safety board sets hearing on ValuJet crash.

text.p: The National Transportation Safety Board scheduled a public hearing on November 18 to gain more information on the crash of a ValuJet Airlines flight in Florida earlier this year, the board said on Wednesday.
The hearing, expected to last five days, will take place at Miami's Radisson Center. The ValuJet DC-9 crashed in the Florida Everglades, near Miami, on May 11, killing all 110 people on board.
The cause has not yet been determined, but investigators say oxygen generators being carried in the aircraft's hold may have ignited, triggering a fire that led to the crash.
Board member John Goglia will preside over the meeting of safety board managers and investigators.
Witnesses will include officials of Valujet, the Federal Aviation Administration, the aircraft's maker McDonnell Douglas Corp., and engine-maker Pratt & Whitney, a unit of United Technologies Corp..

"In this day and age, accidents like this one just should not happen, and I expect this public meeting will provide additional valuable information to aid us in our investigation and prevent future accidents," Goglia said in a statement.

After the crash, the FAA intensified an investigation of the low-cost airline that had already been under way. On June 17, it grounded the carrier's fleet of 51 planes, citing widespread safety violations of maintenance regulations.
Valujet was allowed to resume flying on September 26, although with limited operations.
The FAA gave its approval on the condition that ValuJet retrain its pilots, instructors and maintenance personel and reduce the number of outside contractors used for maintenance and repair.
